To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in vitro dialysis of proteins and protein hydrolysates is a suitable method to investigate the availability of iron and that the type, concentration, and molecular weight of protein digestion products influence iron availability.
The in vitro availability of extrinsic Fe and Zn was affected by the type and concentration of protein.

the type and concentration of protein affect the dialysable Fe and Zn and this could be explained in terms of the effect of the protein on the dialysis of inorganic Fe and Zn and also on the availability of extrinsic Fe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects on in vitro availability of Fe and Zn of the type, level, and fractions of digestion of the protein.
the effects of the type (meat, fish and vegetable), concentration (10, 20 and 30 g) and fraction (high and low molecular weight) of protein on the in vitro availability of Fe and Zn.
the effect of the type, amount and fractions of digestion product of the protein on the availability of Fe and Zn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the type and level of proteins affect the in vitro dialysability of non-haem Fe and Zn and that the effect of the protein on the dialysabilty of Fe is related to its ability to form complexes with Fe.
the in vitro availability of extrinsic Fe and Zn is influenced by the type and concentration of protein, and that the availability of intrinsic Fe depends on the type of protein.
the in viro dialysability of Fe and Zn from proteins depends on the type of protein, the level of protein and the type of Fe and Zn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the availability of intrinsic Fe and Zn from the protein was not affected by the presence of inorganic Zn, while the availability of extrinsic Fe was significantly reduced in the presence of inogamic Zn, especially when the protein was of the soyabean variety.
the dialysis method can be considered as a useful technique to evaluate the effect of proteins and their digestion products on the availability of Fe and Zn.
the dialysability and hence the availability of Fe and Zn from proteins are affected by the type and the amount of protein present in the test meal, as well as by the presence of inorganic Zn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dialysability method can be used as a screening method to evaluate the effect of the type and level of the protein on the in vitro dialysability of Fe and Zn.
in order to better understand the role of protein on the absorption process of Fe, the type of protein, the protein level and the fractions of digestion products should be taken into consideration.

the in vitro dialysis technique is an excellent tool for the study of the availability of Fe and Zn from foodstuffs and that this method can be used to investigate the effects of different food components on the absorption of Fe and Zn.
